per_case_results.query: As a central government employee, how is the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation determined?
per_case_results.direct_answer: For a Central Government employee, the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation is calculated as the License Fee determined by the Central Government in accordance with its allotment rules, reduced by the actual rent paid by the employee. If the accommodation is furnished, the value is increased by 10% per annum of the original cost of furniture/appliances (or actual hire charges if hired from a third party), reduced by any furniture charges paid by the employee.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Applies as per Rule 3 amendments effective September 1, 2023, relevant for Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25) onwards.

citations.citation_text: Where accommodation is provided by Central Government or State Government: License fee determined by Government as reduced by rent actually paid by employee. For furnished accommodation, increased by 10% p.a. of cost of furniture or actual hire charges, reduced by charges paid by employee.
For government employees serving on deputation with any body or undertaking under control of Government, the perquisite value shall be calculated in accordance with Sl. No. (2)(a) of Table I.

matched_criteria: Refers to licence fee determined by the Government
Mentions deduction of rent actually paid by employee

per_case_results.query: I am a private company employee living in a town with a population of 12 lakhs. My employer owns the apartment provided to me. What percentage of my salary is taken as the accommodation perk under the 1962 rules?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under the Income-tax Rules, 1962 (as amended effective September 1, 2023), the perquisite value for employer-owned unfurnished accommodation in a city with a population of 12 lakhs (which falls into the 'other areas' category of 15 lakhs or less) is 5% of your salary for the period the accommodation is occupied, as reduced by any rent actually paid by you.

per_case_results.query: I am a senior citizen aged 77 who receives only pension and interest income. Can I submit a declaration to my bank under Rule 26D so that no tax return is required to be filed?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Yes, a senior citizen aged 77 who receives only pension and interest income can submit a declaration under Rule 26D of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 to avoid filing a formal tax return. The declaration must be furnished to the designated bank using Form No. 12BBA, after which the bank will compute total income and deduct tax under Chapter VI-A.

per_case_results.query: I changed jobs during the previous year. What form must I submit to my current employer to declare salary and TDS from my previous employer under Rule 26A?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 26A of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, the employee must furnish details of income from their previous employer to their current employer using either Form No. 16 (for total salary not exceeding ₹1,50,000) or Form No. 12BA (for total salary exceeding ₹1,50,000). These forms must be submitted directly to the person responsible for making the payment (i.e., the current employer).
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: This provision applies to the Financial Year (FY) in which the change of employment occurred. Rule 26A has no effective date restriction (listed as 'None'), meaning it was in full force throughout the relevant period under the 1962 regime. The assessment year (AY) corresponding to a given fiscal year follows the standard convention (e.g., FY 2019-20 corresponds to AY 2020-21).

per_case_results.query: How did the Leave Travel Concession (LTC) exemption rules change between Rule 2B of the 1962 rules and Rule 278 of the 2026 rules regarding block years?
per_case_results.direct_answer: The primary change between the 1962 Rule 2B and 2026 Rule 278 LTC exemption rules is the specific temporal anchoring of the block year. Under the 1962 rules, the exemption could be claimed for any journey within a general 'block of four calendar years' without a fixed starting point. In contrast, the 2026 Rule 278 explicitly limits the exemption to 'two journeys performed in a block of four calendar years commencing from the calendar year 2022.' Additionally, the 2026 rules introduce a Rs. 30 per kilometre rate for non-rail journeys when no recognized public transport system exists, and impose a cap of two surviving children for the exemption. These represent significant refinements in both the scope and methodology compared to the 1962 framework.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Both the 1962 Rule 2B and 2026 Rule 278 provisions are generally applicable to financial years where a block of four consecutive calendar years can be identified. For the 2026 rules, there is a specific temporal constraint: the exemption is limited to journeys within a block of four calendar years commencing from the calendar year 2022 (i.e., FY 2022-23 through FY 2025-26 and beyond). The 1962 rules do not specify a starting year, allowing the block to span any four consecutive calendar years.

The amount exempted... shall be the amount actually incurred on the performance of such travel, subject to conditions on air, rail, and other modes of transport. The exemption... shall be available to an individual in respect of two journeys performed in a block of four calendar years commencing from the calendar year 2022.

per_case_results.direct_answer: For Financial Year 2021-22 (Assessment Year 2022-2023), the special compensatory border allowance is governed by Rule 2BB > (1) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 (effective 23-09-2015). Rule 2BB > (3) (effective 21-06-2023) does not apply as it became effective after FY 2021-22. Therefore, the exemptions for special compensatory allowances (including border area allowances) are determined solely by the provisions in Rule 2BB > (1), which specify the allowed amounts and geographic scopes for different regions.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Financial Year 2021-22 (Assessment Year 2022-2023) – Rule 2BB > (1) (effective 23-09-2015) is fully applicable. Rule 2BB > (3) (effective 21-06-2023) is not applicable as it became effective after the fiscal year ended.

per_case_results.query: I am a salaried individual filing an Updated Return (ITR-U) under Rule 12AC. My accounts are not required to be audited, and I do NOT have a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC). How am I permitted to verify my return according to the table in Rule 12AC?
per_case_results.direct_answer: As a salaried individual whose accounts are not required to be audited under section 44AB, you may file your Updated Return (Form ITR-U) using the 'electronic verification code' method. You do not need a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) for this approach. Under Rule 12AC of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, persons whose case accounts are not subject to audit (including individuals, Hindu undivided families, firms, limited liability partnerships, and associations) may transmit their return data electronically in the return under an electronic verification code. This allows verification without requiring a DSC.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Rule 12AC applies to Assessment Years (AY) commencing on 1st April 2020 and subsequent years (e.g., AY 2021-22, AY 2022-23, etc.). The effective date of Rule 12AC is 29-04-2022. Your Updated Return (ITR-U) for AY 2021-22 or later will be governed by this rule. For earlier assessment years (before 2021-22), different rules may apply.

per_case_results.query: What specific form must a salaried employee furnish to their employer under Rule 26C to claim tax deductions for House Rent Allowance (HRA), Leave Travel Concession (LTC), and home loan interest?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 26C of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, a salaried employee must furnish the evidence or particulars of their claims for House Rent Allowance (HRA), Leave Travel Concession (LTC), and home loan interest deduction using **Form No. 12BB**. This form is used to provide the necessary documentation to the employer (person responsible for making payment under section 192) for estimating income and computing tax deduction at source.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: This provision under Rule 26C of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 applies to the Assessment Year (AY) corresponding to the Financial Year (FY) when the claim is made. Since there is no effective date restriction mentioned for Rule 26C, it remains in full force for all relevant assessment years under the 1962 regime.
